summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, flank pain, and purulent drainage from his left nephrostomy tube site, consistent with cellulitis and complicated cystitis. He had a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder with ileal conduit, chronic kidney disease, and recurrent urinary infections. Initial treatment with IV meropenem was complicated by a mild rash, managed with antihistamines. Blood cultures were negative, and later urine cultures showed no growth. The infection resolved after a 7-day course of antibiotics. He was transitioned to suppressive oral fosfomycin therapy and discharged home in stable condition. A nephrostomy tube exchange was scheduled for outpatient follow-up. His chronic conditions, including pain, anxiety, and anemia, were managed throughout the stay.
